ana.t: Quick note from ops: we keep seeing claim collisions + skipped owners when enrichment tails spike. Idea: add a short grace window with jitter around the RR claim timeout, then fallback to overflow pool. Should reduce churn and give enrichment a tiny breathing room. Thoughts?
kevin.l: Sounds promising. How would the jitter work with HubSpot workflows?
maya.r: We can push a `routing_timeout_secs` property and a `routing_jitter_secs` property per campaign. The claim flow: 1) wait timeout + random(0, jitter) 2) if still not enriched -> mark `fastlane=true` and assign to overflow RR.
jon.s: SDRs: prefer the overflow pool to be a named queue with a short SLA (e.g., 30m) so they know these leads may miss some enrichment. Tooltip/help doc please.
hubspot-bot: Created test property `routing_timeout_secs` and `routing_jitter_secs` in sandbox. :white_check_mark:
ana.t (typo): ^^ ana^^
kevin.l: Can you share a config example?
maya.r: Sure — sketch below:
```yaml
routing_policy:
  campaigns_opt_in: ["ebook-gated","trial-start"]
  timeout_seconds: 20
  jitter_seconds: 6
  fallback_queue: "sdr-overflow-quick"
  set_properties:
    fastlane: "true"
    routing_reason: "timeout+jitter"
  recheck_enrichment_after: 300  # seconds to patch record after enrich completes
```
kevin.l: Nice. For randomness use secure PRNG to avoid predictability of claim order. Also cap jitter to 50% of timeout.
jon.s: Ops ask: when a lead is assigned to overflow we need a HS task template: "Quick qualify (fastlane)" and a checkbox "enrichment-pending". SDRs will mark when done so we can re-run enrichment.
maya.r: Good call. Also let's set a SF flag `DoNotMerge=true` and `Lead_Source="fastlane_jitter"` while pending. routing-monitor-bot: Hook created: lead-routing-heartbeat -> emits `claim_latency_ms` and `fastlane_count` per campaign.
nana.t (typo again): sorry for name spam
ana.t: (sigh)
ana.t: (really)
kevin.l: For rollout: 1) sandbox test publish properties 2) run 2k simulated leads with tail noise (/tools/lead-sim --campaign ebook-gated --count 2000 --tail-prob 0.015 --tail-latency 55) 3) enable in read-only mode (set props but don't assign) 4) enable assignment for single low-risk campaign 5) monitor `fastlane_rate` and `owner_claim_success`.
maya.r: I ran the sim: static 15s fallback -> 2.5% fastlane. With timeout=20 + jitter=6 -> 1.1% fastlane and fewer owner skips. Logs: https://internal/ci/lead-jitter/2955
jon.s: If sim looks good, we want a short SDR training doc and a Slack workflow to tag urgent fastlane leads to #sdr-urgent.
hubspot-bot: Workflow draft created: fastlane-jitter-assign (id: wf_20260323_jitter_test).
kevin.l: Add alerting: page marketing oncall if fastlane_rate > 1.5% on revenue campaigns, or if re-enrichment patch rate < 70% after 1 hour.
maya.r: I'll add dashboard panels and alert rules. I'll also include the SQL we used for tail calc in the RFC.
jon.s: Final ask: when enrichment completes after a fastlane assign, please append a note to lead: "enrichment completed post-assign; do not reassign owner". Avoid churn. routing-monitor-bot: Note appended automation rule queued. :gear:
nana.t: ok let's file the RFC and schedule canary next Tue for ebook-gated. I'll draft the SDR help doc and ping the leads. :rocket:
